Lessons.Title: What is an Angle?
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will introduce angles and to motivate a need for vocabulary to describe what you are and your size.
In this lesson, you are introduced to angles. You learn that an angle can be defined in terms of the geometric parts you have been working with in this unit. In previous grades, you have used “square corners” to describe right angles within two-dimensional shapes.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: A Wall of Clocks (5 minutes); Activity 1: Tricky Figures (15 minutes); Activity 2: Angles or Not Angles? (15 minutes); Activity 3: Discover Angles (10 minutes); Cool-down: Spot the Angles (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: An angle consists of two rays with the same endpoint (vertex); its size is the amount of turning, not ray length.

Edulytics authored guidance: Use the original examples to decide whether two rays share a common vertex. Mark the vertex and arms of each valid angle. Explain why separated segments need not form an angle unless their rays share a vertex.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Draw two rays PA and PB starting at P, mark the angle APB.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
